solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put sign up for submarine captain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: An instruction to hoist a signal on behalf of a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo is the fictional commander of the Nautilus in the Jules Verne novel.

indicators.note: rigs that have collapsed are in pieces, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Some oil rigs fell down, and the observer remarks they are no longer twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not bent is straight, the plain antonym of curved or crooked.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: joined together as one
second meaning: many English football clubs are called ..., such as Manchester ...

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the team is only one example among the many clubs with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined as a single body, and also the usual short name for clubs like Manchester United or Leeds United.

clue.text: Company, extremely loyal, that is dog

indicators.note: extremely asks for only the extreme letters of loyal, its first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of loyal
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A business describes its very faithful companion, a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is the stock crossword signal for the Latin abbreviation i.e. (id est).
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Old saw that's lost its edge?

definitions.text: Old saw that's lost its edge?

parts.words: Old saw that's lost its edge?
parts.note: a saw is also a saying; an old saying that has lost its sharpness through overuse is a worn-out phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a blunt carpenter's tool, but a saw is also a proverb, and one blunted by repetition is hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliche is a hackneyed expression whose force has been dulled by overuse, like a blunt saying.

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Punishing the black sheep of the family with a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black sheep' reads as the family outcast, but black gives B and sheep is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is a young sheep, so the definition names its species.

clue.text: Phone system Bury firm marketed at first

parts.note: to inter is to bury
CO, company, is a firm

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of marketed

parts.note: first letter of marketed

explanation.surface: A telephone system sold by a company in Bury, the town near Manchester, was first on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is capitalised to look like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb meaning inter.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal communication system, a kind of phone link between rooms.

indicators.note: the phrase absent in electrical stores, or holds, the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A security guard who is missing from his post in an electrical shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electrical stores' looks like shops selling appliances; stores is the verb, keeping the answer inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or watchman standing guard.

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: Someone held in jail in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is capitalised to suggest the country; in cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a person confined in a prison or institution.

indicators.note: ridiculously says the letters of minor act are treated absurdly, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic says a small stage act is absurdly soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic can mean idealised or emotional in a soft, mawkish way, matching sentimental.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mog or moggy is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A little cat glimpsed through the murky city air.
explanation.walkthrough: A mog, or moggy, is informal British for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is a polluted fog typical of cities, so it is a haze over urban areas.

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters of unit some are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A Canadian police unit in which some officers are corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' looks part of the definition, but it is anagram fodder with 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mounties is the popular name for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

parts.note: to slim is to diet
well-to-do means rich

explanation.surface: An actress who is described as thin and wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born Hollywood film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a famous film star of the 1930s and later, so she is an actress.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: frozen water, used to chill things

explanation.walkthrough: 'cool stuff' reads as slang praise for trendy things, but it is literal: stuff that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds and is also frozen water used for chilling drinks.

parts.note: rocks means shocks or stuns
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer astonishes a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock star is a celebrated performer of rock music, so a famous musician.

clue.text: Person you deal with in scrum with toe broken

indicators.note: broken says the letters of scrum and toe are shattered and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A rugby player injured his toe in a scrum, and someone in business looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is a client you do business with, a buyer you serve.

clue.text: Painter outside grand bar that's attractive

indicators.note: outside says the painter's name sits around the letter for grand

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French painter
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An artist standing outside a fancy bar, finding it appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand bar' looks like a smart pub; grand gives G, and bar belongs to the definition, the bar shape of many magnets.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet, often a metal bar, attracts iron, so it is a bar with attraction.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, so the range comes on top of the run

parts.note: a range is a line of mountains
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A commando soldier in the mountains, out running.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers are US Army special forces, elite assault troops like commandos.

indicators.note: covering means the horse's letters wrap around the abbreviation for miles

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A horse covering many miles while out searching.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as if with the teeth of a comb.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A painful red eye with some kind of swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of the answer, and the question mark admits the hidden word is also its own example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid.

clue.text: Guy's initial anxiety on about criminal

indicators.note: initial asks for only the first letter of Guy's

parts.note: first letter of Guy's
angst is anxiety or dread

indicators.note: about says the word for on turns around

parts.note: re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A man's first bout of nerves about a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' here means concerning, as in the 're:' heading of a letter, and 'about' turns that word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised gang of violent criminals.

clue.text: Make an impression and so on with Henry

parts.note: etc. is short for et cetera, and so on
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone making their mark, and similar things, together with a man called Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design, making an impression on a surface.

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for obsessed

parts.note: smitten means infatuated, obsessed

explanation.surface: Someone besotted lets a glove slip away for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like the timing of the loss; it is S, removed from SMITTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a kind of glove with a single section for the four fingers.

clue.text: English cricket side win at last in great style

parts.note: leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side behind the batsman's legs

indicators.note: in says the final letter of win goes inside the word for great

parts.note: ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: at last asks for only the final letter of win

parts.note: last letter of win

explanation.surface: England's cricket team wins at last, in fine fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side (or on side) is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is graceful refinement, the quality of having style.

indicators.note: verbal points to a spoken version, a word sounding the same as the word for agreement

parts.note: assent is agreement

explanation.surface: A spoken agreement to a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward movement, a rise in height.
